notesStmt.note: Whitman's note at the bottom of this draft gives the specific date of its creation: May 10, 1890.
"On, On the Same, Ye Jocund Twain!" was first published in Good-Bye My Fancy, in May 1891. It also appeared shortly thereafter in the 9 June 1891 issue of the magazine Once a Week.

lg.head: On, on the same, ye jocund twain!
lg.l: On, on the same, ye jocund twain!

My life and recitative, combining continuing birth, youth,
mid-age years,

Fitful as ‸motley tongues of flame inseperably twined
and merged in one;‸—combining all,

My single soul—aims, confirmations, failures, joys—
nor single soul, ‸in these, alone,

‸I chant My nation's crucial stage, (America's, hu-
manity'shumanity's
,)—the trial great, the victory great,

A strange ecclairecissementéclaircissement of ‸all the masses, past the
eastern world, the ancient, medieval;

Here, here, from wanderings, strayings, lessons,
wars, defeats—here at the west a voice
triumphant—justifying all,

A gladsome pealing cry—a song ‸for once of utmost of pride and
satisfaction;

I chant, ‸from it, the race, the common bulk, the general
average horde (the best no sooner than
the worst)—and now I chant old age,

(My verses, written first for earl forenoon life,
and for the summer's, autumn's spread,

I pass to snow-white hairs the same, and give to
pulses winter cool'd the same;)

As now, here, in carelesss ‸trill, chant,
‸I and my recitative, myself, with faith
and love,
Wafteding to other work, to unknown joys, songs, conditions,
On, on, ye jocund twain! continue on, the same!
